hero.title: Built-in communications and e-signature
hero.description: Sttok emails notices and notifications to shareholders and directors, with proof of delivery. Documents are signed with DocuSign without leaving Sttok, signatures are placed automatically above each name, and everything signed is filed in the company records. Everything is logged.

setup.title: Communicate, sign and file, on the same platform
setup.lede: No jumping between email, the signing tool and folders: every step stays with the company it belongs to.

steps.title: Communicate
steps.text: Notices, messages and reminders to shareholders and directors, by email, with the company's sender name and logo. Every delivery comes with its certificate: to whom, when and with what result.

steps.title: Sign
steps.text: DocuSign is built into Sttok: minutes, certificates and any other document are sent for signature without leaving Sttok. Sttok suggests the signers and places every signature above each name in one click. You can see who has signed and who has not, and remind pending signers right there.

steps.title: File
steps.text: Signed documents are filed automatically in their folder: minutes in the minute book; proxies and certificates in the company records. Every delivery comes with its certificate and the log keeps every delivery and signature with its date and time.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about communications and signatures

items.q: Do I need a separate DocuSign account?
items.a: No. DocuSign signing is built into Sttok: the document is sent for signature from the company itself and each signer receives the DocuSign email.
The Advanced and Pro plans. Email communications and their proof of delivery are in every plan.

items.q: Do emails go out in the company's name?
items.a: Yes. Communications go out with the company's email signature and logo, and the recipient knows who to reply to.

items.q: What does the delivery certificate show?
items.a: Who it was sent to, when and with what result: delivered and bounced. Sttok issues it from the log of each delivery, and it can be downloaded as a PDF.

items.q: Do I have to place the signatures by hand on each document?
items.a: No. Documents generated by Sttok, such as the minutes, already know where each person signs. On your own PDF, Sttok finds each signer's name and places their signature above it; if it cannot find one, it says so and you place it by hand.

items.q: Where do signed documents end up?
items.a: In the company records, next to the meeting, board meeting or transaction they come from. The signed minutes go into the minute book with one click.
